(Search snippet content — CNN / Al Jazeera / Times of Israel, 7–8 August 2026, own reporting language)

Mecca Joint Defence (Deterrence) Agreement, signed in Mecca on Friday 7 August 2026:
- Signatories: Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan, Saudi Crown Prince and PM Mohammed bin Salman, Pakistani PM Shehbaz Sharif.
- Treats an armed attack on any one member as an attack on all — similar to NATO's Article 5. Pakistan's Foreign Ministry said the pact meant an attack on any member would be regarded as an attack on all, "intended to strengthen collective deterrence".
- Unites Turkey (NATO's second-largest army), Saudi Arabia (top oil exporter) and Pakistan (only Muslim-majority nuclear power).
- Follows nearly a year of negotiations. Analysts: pact "essentially puts three of the largest Muslim populations together", marking a "different security architecture".
- Nuclear ambiguity: experts say the accord would likely NOT include a nuclear component (Pakistan's deterrent focused on India); Saudi officials asked whether it extends a nuclear umbrella answered elliptically, describing "all military means" without disavowing the nuclear question.
- CNN 8 Aug live blog headline: "Saudi Arabia, Turkey and Pakistan sign NATO-style defense pact amid widening Iran conflict."
